_about: Demo E (four different connections). Single source for the static panels in m05.html (written by scripts/invisible_engine/content/inserts.py) and for connections.js; tested by invisible-engine/tests/demos.mjs. Labels: doc = Apple-documented behaviour; concept = our generic explanation; verify = check the current Apple page.

tabs.label: Setup and account registration
tabs.who: The tag and the owner’s iPhone or iPad, then the owner’s Apple Account.
tabs.link: Bluetooth between tag and phone; the internet between phone and Apple.
tabs.pairs: Yes. The owner taps Connect and links the tag to one Apple Account.
tabs.moves: Setup messages and the keys the owner’s devices will use later. The message-level detail is not publicly documented.
tabs.learns: Apple records that the item belongs to the account. The owner’s devices hold the keys.
tabs.not: Not something a stranger’s phone can do: a tag already linked to an account cannot simply be added to another.

tabs.label: Crowdsourced sighting
tabs.who: The tag whispers; any participating passer-by’s Apple device overhears; the sealed report goes to the relay; the owner’s device fetches it later.
tabs.link: Bluetooth Low Energy advertising (listen-only), then the finder’s internet connection.
tabs.range: Bluetooth range: metres to tens of metres, depending on walls, bodies and interference.
tabs.pairs: No. The finder only overhears a broadcast; there is no handshake with the tag.
tabs.moves: A changing identifier over the air; then a report encrypted to that identifier, filed under its lookup value.
tabs.learns: The finder learns nothing about the owner. The relay stores ciphertext and metadata. The owner’s device decrypts an estimated location and a time.
tabs.not: Not live tracking: reports arrive when, and if, a participating device passes by.

tabs.label: Nearby Precision Finding
tabs.who: The owner’s iPhone (or a shared user’s) and the tag, face to face.
tabs.link: Bluetooth to find and wake the tag; ultra-wideband ranging for distance and direction, combined with the phone’s camera and motion sensors.
tabs.range: Nearby: within Bluetooth range of the tag.
tabs.pairs: Only the owner’s devices, or people the owner shares the item with.
tabs.moves: Ranging exchanges between the two devices: timing, from which distance and direction are calculated on the phone.
tabs.learns: The owner’s phone learns how far and in which direction the tag is. Nobody learns a map position from this.
tabs.not: Not a global location: an arrow and a distance, not a pin on a map. Requires an iPhone with ultra-wideband (iPhone 11 and later, excluding iPhone SE models).
tabs.source: Apple Support, “Locate an AirTag with Precision Finding”.

tabs.label: Lost Mode NFC
tabs.who: Anyone who finds the tag, with an NFC-capable smartphone (iPhone or Android), and a web page from Apple.
tabs.link: NFC tap, then the finder’s browser over the internet.
tabs.range: A few centimetres: the phone touches the tag.
tabs.pairs: No. The tap opens a web page.
tabs.moves: The tag’s serial number and, if the owner turned on Lost Mode, the message and contact details the owner chose to share.
tabs.learns: The finder sees only what the owner chose to show. The owner can be notified when the item is found.
tabs.not: Not distant tracking: NFC works only when touching, and adds nothing to the crowdsourced network.
tabs.source: Apple Support, “Put an AirTag in Lost Mode” (verify current wording).
